limitations_and_boundaries: DeepONet accuracy is bounded by the numerical solver used to generate training data.
Training DeepONets is computationally intensive because the dataset size is the product of the number of input functions and evaluation locations.
Theoretical understanding of why DeepONets induce small generalization errors is lacking.
The current work uses fully connected neural networks for subnetworks; other architectures like CNNs or attention may improve accuracy.
The study only considers operators with known mathematical forms; discovering operators from multi-fidelity or heterogeneous data is future work.

research_questions.statement: How can deep neural networks be designed to accurately learn linear and nonlinear operators mapping input functions to output functions?

provenance.text_excerpt: In this Article, we propose a general deep learning framework, DeepONet, to learn diverse continuous nonlinear operators.

claims.statement: DeepONet is a general deep learning framework that can learn diverse continuous nonlinear operators.

provenance.text_excerpt: We will demonstrate that, unlike fully connected neural networks (FNNs) and residual neural networks (ResNets), DeepONet substantially improves generalization based on a design of two subnetworks, the branch net for the input function and the trunk net for the locations to evaluate the output function.

claims.statement: DeepONet substantially improves generalization compared to FNNs and ResNets.

experiments_or_tasks: Compare DeepONet with baseline models (FNN, ResNet, CNN, RNN) on learning explicit and implicit operators.
Design a deep operator network (DeepONet) architecture consisting of a branch net for encoding the discrete input function space and a trunk net for encoding the domain of the output functions.
Extend the universal approximation theorem for operators to deep neural networks (Theorem 2).

methods.name: DeepONet
methods.protocol_description: DeepONet consists of a branch network that takes sensor values [u(x1),...,u(xm)] of the input function and outputs a vector [b1,...,bp], and a trunk network that takes the output location y and outputs [t1,...,tp]. The operator is approximated as G(u)(y) ≈ Σ_{k=1}^p b_k t_k + b0. Both subnetworks are deep neural networks. Training minimizes mean squared error between true G(u)(y) and prediction.

methods.protocol_description: Baseline model that concatenates [u(x1),...,u(xm), y] as input and directly outputs G(u)(y).

methods.protocol_description: Baseline model using residual connections with concatenated input [u(x1),...,u(xm), y].
